question: Which taxa carrying this domain in the known protein universe are absent from this database?

external_universe.label: ring-hydroxylating oxygenase alpha subunit, catalytic domain (Rieske non-haem iron oxygenase family)
external_universe.source: InterPro API, UniProtKB proteins matching the Pfam entry

method.why_not_sequence: the two sides do not count the same unit: InterPro counts one UniProtKB record per protein (a hundred strains carrying the same protein give a hundred records), while this database counts one genome-derived entry; a ratio of two different counting rules is not a coverage measure. A taxid, by contrast, is the same thing on both sides.
method.genus_rule: the nearest ancestor whose NCBI rank is exactly 'genus'; decided by taxonomy_ids.genus_from_ranks, the single owner of the genus question
method.our_denominator: replicons carrying at least one confirmed member (ro.is_confirmed=1)

scope.why: PF00848 is not bacterial: the same domain occurs in plant and fungal choline monooxygenase, while this database is built from bacterial genomes. Without the split, the missing-taxon count is inflated by lineages this database never targeted, so what is measured stops being a coverage gap and becomes a scope definition.
scope.transcript_only_superkingdom_excluded: Eukaryota enters this database only through 958 XM_/NM_ mRNA records and no eukaryotic genome; counting it as scope would put a fungus at the top of the missing list

what_this_is_not: A genus absent from PF00848 is not a genus without the enzyme: not being represented in UniProtKB is an absence of evidence.
A genus present here but absent from PF00848 is not an error: our hits come from the project's own model at its own threshold, not from the Pfam gathering threshold.
The missing-genus list is a proposed download list, not an error list; it is ordered by how many proteins would be gained.

gap.where_the_gap_is: depth (more proteins inside genera already covered)
